sentences.text:
Jagdish Chandra Gupta vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 7
August, 2025

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal Nos.893-894/2016
 Jagdish Chandra Gupta & Anr. Etc. Appel
 Versus
 The State Of Uttar Pradesh Respo
 O R D E R
1. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. The appellants before us were convicted by the Trial Court for the offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the IPC) and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, and sentenced to Date: 2025.08.18 undergo rigorous imprisonment for life, and fine.
The High Court, vide the impugned order, has confirmed the same.
Aggrieved, the appellants are before us.
The appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 893/2016 are the in-laws of the deceased and the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 894/2016 is the husband of the deceased.
3. We have perused the impugned judgment.

sentences.text: Insofar as the appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 893/2016 are concerned, we find absolutely no material to implicate them for the allegation of demand of dowry soon before the death of the deceased.
Merely because they are the in-laws, the demand of dowry cannot be stated to have been proven.
No evidence has been adduced to prove that they subjected the deceased to cruelty.
In such view of the matter, the provisions under which they were charged are not attracted.
Thus, we are inclined to set aside the impugned judgment qua the said appellants.
Accordingly, the conviction rendered against the appellants - Jagdish Chandra and Munni Devi, stands set aside and they are acquitted of all charges.
5. Insofar as the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 894/2016 is concerned, on a perusal of the records, we find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment qua him.
Witnesses have clearly implicated him with respect to the demand of dowry.
Admittedly, the deceased died within one year of the marriage, and the occurrence took place in the matrimonial home.
Therefore, both the Courts have rightly drawn the presumption against the said appellant.

6. However, taking into consideration the fact that he has undergone approximately 11 years of incarceration, and that the occurrence was of the year 1998, we are inclined to modify his sentence to the period already undergone.
Accordingly, while confirming the conviction, the sentence of the appellant - Sanjiv Kumar @ Boby, stands modified to the period already undergone.
7. Thus, Criminal Appeal No. 893/2016 stands allowed, and Criminal Appeal No. 894/2016 stands allowed in part.
8. The bail bonds, if any, stand discharged.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
J . [ M . M . S U N D R E S H ]
J. [JOYMALYA BAGCHI] NEW DELHI;
